newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel ready to meet German SPD at any time on tax.
newsitem.headline: Waigel ready to meet German SPD at any time on tax.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday he was ready at any time to resume talks on tax reforms with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD).
"I am ready for tax talks with the SPD at any time," Waigel told a news conference where he presented a legislative draft of the government's plans to cut 30 billion marks in tax.
But Waigel said he was not prepared to accept any new preconditions from the SPD, who he accused of pulling out of tax negotiations a week ago for "tactical political reasons".

The SPD quit negotiations in sympathy with coal miners protesting at government plans to cut coal subsidies, but that row was settled on Thursday when Chancellor Helmut Kohl and miners' leaders reached a compromise agreement.
Waigel said he was still waiting for concrete proposals from the SPD to match the coalition plan which was agreed back in January.

He added that the coalition tax reform would cut a gross 84 billion marks, mainly in income and corporate taxes, in 1998 and 1999. Those cuts would be offset by abolishing some 45.5 billion marks in tax breaks.
Waigel has said that a part of the remaining revenue shortfall could be made up through a one-point increase in Germany's 15 percent rate of value-added tax.
The goal of the reform must be to open the way to more growth and new jobs by cutting German tax rates which are too high compared to other countries, Waigel said.
